e-4518.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}6x+4y=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & b & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
e-4518.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation:

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x+4y+0z=1 \\ x-8y-z=-2 \\ 3x+2y-2z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & -8 & -1 \\ 3 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, $a=6,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-2.$

e-4519.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ z-x+2=-1 \\ 2y-2x-4z=-4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & a & 1 \\ b & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

What are the values of $a,$ $b$ and $c?$
e-4519.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y+z=4 \\ -x+0y+z=-3 \\ -2x+2y-4z=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore $a=0,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-3.$

$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Entries of a Matrix Product Representing a 3x3 System of Equations by Reorganizing
content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-y+z=1 \\ 2z+y+x=-1 \\ 3y-z+x=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & b \\ 1 & c & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-y+z=1 \\ x+y+2z=-1 \\ x+3y-z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=0,\,b=2,\,c=3.$

after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y-5x+3z=-1 \\ x-3y=3 \\ -3y+2z-x=-5\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5 & a & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & b \\ c & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-5x+2y+3z=-1 \\ x-3y+0z=3 \\ -x-3y+2z=-5\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & -3 & 0 \\ -1 & -3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=2,\,b=0,\,c=-1.$

content.knowledge_point: Identifying Entries of a Matrix Product Representing a 3x3 System of Equations by Reorganizing
content.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y+2z-x=1 \\ 6y+3x-2z=2 \\ x+3z-y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & b & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-x+y+2z=1 \\ 3x+6y-2z=2 \\ x-y+3z=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-1,\,b=6,\,c=-3.$

after.problem:
The system of equations

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2y+3z=7 \\ x+z=-1 \\ 3z-2x+y=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

can be represented using matrix notation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & b & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ c\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the values of $a,b$ and $c?$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that $x$, $y$, and $z$ appear in each equation in the correct order and all constants are on the right-hand side of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-2y+3z=7 \\ x+0y+z=-1 \\ -2x+y+3z=3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=0,\,b=0,\,c=3.$
